sections.title: What to prioritize today
sections.headline: Finish the Friday loaf list before the market opens.
sections.body: Write the bakers' board, then walk the first tray.

recommendations.headline: Finish the Friday loaf list before the market opens
recommendations.body: Saturday's market still has no clear card for the rye, while the tasting flight is already drawing questions at the counter. Make the offer legible before adding another product: a customer who understands the loaf can choose it, describe it, and come back for it.

evidence.claim: The rye still lacks a market card
Customers asked for the tasting flight in writing

recommendations.first_step: Write the rye card and pin it on the board by 09:00.

advisor.name: Patrick Salyer (Mayfield)
advisor.quote: You'll know you're on the right track when you have a handful of referenceable customers ... and a "painkiller" solution.

recommendations.headline: Turn the first tray walk into a repeatable quality check
recommendations.body: The morning tray walk is useful only if tomorrow's baker can repeat what Mira notices today. Capture the few observable signs that distinguish a ready loaf from one that needs another minute, then use the same check before every market batch.

evidence.claim: The first trays are reviewed with Mira

recommendations.first_step: Write the three checks beside the oven before the 09:15 walk.

advisor.name: Patrick Salyer (Mayfield)
advisor.quote: it's crucial for founders to be involved in establishing a sales playbook.

recommendations.headline: Let the tasting flight earn the next packaging spend
recommendations.body: Packaging is a use-of-funds decision; the tasting flight is the milestone that can justify it. Use this weekend to learn which pairing people understand and buy, then spend only against the presentation change that evidence unlocks.

evidence.claim: The tasting flight has active customer interest

recommendations.first_step: Prepare one tasting card with two pairings, one purchase question, and no packaging order.

advisor.name: Patrick Salyer (Mayfield)
advisor.quote: Raise the right amount of money, at a stage appropriate valuation, to hit the milestones that unlock the next stage.

sections.title: City opens the old ferry waiting room as a reading hall
sections.headline: Free tables, long hours, and a view of the channel
sections.body:
Port Meridian converted the unused ferry waiting room into a public reading hall this week, with long tables facing the channel and hours that run past the last boat.

The city says the room had sat empty since the foot-ferry moved to the new pier. Volunteers stocked the shelves from two closing bookshops on Harbor Street.

A Saturday morning paper hour is already on the board: bring a section, leave it for the next reader.

sections.title: Mill workers vote to keep the night shift
sections.headline: Harbor Mill stays on two ovens through winter
sections.body:
Harbor Mill's night crew voted to keep the second shift through March, after a week of counting sacks against winter orders from the inner towns.

The mill posted the result on the dock board at dawn. Bakers on the strip said the extra bags are what Saturday's market has been short of since August.

sections.title: Market adds an early bakers' gate
sections.headline: Saturday setup moves forward by half an hour
sections.body:
Port Market will open the service gate to bakers at 06:30 on Saturday, thirty minutes earlier than last week.

The market coordinator said the change is a trial for the winter schedule. Stallholders must still clear the lane before the public gates open.
